transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start: 15:00 PST
Duration: 60 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Raj Patel (Lumina Head of ML), Ava Morgan (Lumina Platform), Carlos Ruiz (Lumina SecArch), Leah Kim (Product)

Summary (auto):
Quick scoping call to define POC success criteria for latency and throughput SLOs. Focus on TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99 targets, measurement plan, benchmarks and timelines. Action items assigned.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, let's do quick intros then jump into the latency SLOs and how we want to measure them for the POC.
[00:12] Raj: thanks, yeah, we want to validate that any model you serve for us can meet our interactive latency targets — our UX team expects snappy chat responses, so TTFT is important.
[00:23] Omar: totally, and we'll cover TTFT (time to first token) and TPOT, which we're using internally to mean time-per-output-token, so both initial response and steady-state cost/throughput matter.
[00:34] Ava: quick question — do you measure TPOT as ms/token, or tokens-per-second? we use tps for capacity planning, so whichever you provide we can convert.
[00:44] Priya: we typically report both: TPOT as ms per token (median/p95/p99) and tokens/sec under sustained load for throughput. for capacity planning we'll give tokens/sec at target latency bound.
[00:57] Carlos: security quick note — we'll need SOC 2, SSO, audit logs, KMS details for encryption-at-rest and in-transit, and we'd like to see how Redwood exposes trace IDs for correlating traces with our logs.
[01:12] Maya: good, we'll share SOC2 and KMS docs. Omar will add tracing hooks in the benchmark harness.
[01:20] Raj: for success criteria — high level: TTFT p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 400ms for our short prompts (<= 64 tokens). For longer multi-turn contexts we'd accept higher TTFT but want TPOT p95 <= 20ms/token and p99 <= 50ms/token. these are starting numbers.
[01:39] Maya: that's helpful. can you describe typical prompt distribution? mean, p50, p95 token lengths, and what percent of requests are single-turn vs multi-turn?
[01:50] Raj: sure — average prompt ~ 42 tokens, p95 ~ 210 tokens, only about 12% are > 300 tokens. single-turn is about 60% of requests, 30% are short multi-turn (2-3 turns), 10% are longer sessions.
[02:08] Leah: also want cost context — we care about the cost per active user and how batching / quantization tradeoffs affect quality.
[02:17] Omar: absolutely — the POC will include measured unit economics across a few model configs: hosted baseline, quantized variant, and a dedicated pool configuration. we'll measure latency and tokens/sec and link to cost estimates.
[02:29] Ava: how do you account for warm vs cold cache? our workload has lots of repeated prefixes for product Q&A.
[02:36] Priya: we'll run two benchmark phases: cold start runs and warm runs with cache/KV primed. we'll collect TTFT and TPOT histograms, and also report cold-start percent of traffic.
[02:47] Raj: good. on SLOs — we need both latency SLOs (TTFT/TPOT p95/p99) and throughput SLOs (tokens/sec or concurrent requests at given SLO). e.g., we might need 100 concurrent users with 1.5 RPS each and 90 tokens per response on average.
[03:05] Omar: can you confirm expected qps / concurrency?
[03:09] Raj: for the POC target let's assume 150 concurrent sessions, 1.2 RPS average, target average response 80 tokens — so rough sustained tokens/sec about 150 * 1.2 * 80 = 14,400 tokens/sec. but we'll validate with your run.
[03:27] Maya: ok we'll size the benchmark to hit that sustained token rate plus 2x spike tests.
[03:32] Carlos: curious about parsing TPOT at tail percentiles — do you aggregate per-request time-per-token or measure token emission latency series?
[03:40] Priya: we capture token emission times per-request, compute per-request TPOT median and then build distribution across requests to compute p95/p99 of TPOT. we also compute p95/p99 of TTFT across requests.
[03:53] Raj: perfect. also need to tie model variant to results — if you fallback to a cheaper model we need automatic annotation in logs.
[04:01] Omar: yes, we'll include model_variant, instance_type, batch_size, and cache_state in each measurement row. those will be in the benchmark output csv.
[04:10] Ava: on measurement tooling — what do you run? custome harness? k6? wrk?
[04:17] Omar: internal harness built on go with configurable inter-arrival and token-emission tracking; for transparency we'll give the script and a Docker image. it records TTFT, per-token deltas, and server-side timestamps when available.
[04:30] Maya: we'll also provide a spreadsheet that maps model config to cost/node and expected tokens/sec.
[04:36] Leah: timeline wise — what's realistic for a two-week POC?
[04:41] Maya: propose this: week 0 (this week) — agreement on prompts and SLOs; week 1 — baseline benchmark (hosted) + priming runs; week 2 — optimizations (quantization/dedicated pool tweaks) and final report. so about 2 weeks total, with a checkpoint at end of week 1.
[04:58] Raj: that works; we might need one more week if network peering for private deployment takes time but we'll try to keep within 3 weeks.
[05:07] Carlos: for security review we may need to run scans — will you allow a short security interview and a scan of the benchmark endpoints?
[05:15] Maya: yes, we'll coordinate with your security team. we typically do a limited-scope scan in a staging environment.
[05:22] Ava: spike test details? we want 2x and 5x bursts to see graceful degradation and fallback behaviors.
[05:29] Priya: we'll include steady-state at target, 2x surge, and short 5x spike. we'll collect error rates, queueing latency, and tail metrics, and show fallback counts if model variant fallback triggers.
[05:41] Raj: fallback behavior: prefer to degrade to a slightly smaller model variant with explicit annotation, rather than dropping requests. need to see expected quality drop.
[05:50] Omar: we'll include automated A/B quality checks on sampled outputs using your eval set to quantify quality regression when fallback occurs.
[05:58] Maya: recap of success criteria as I heard it: TTFT p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 400ms for short prompts; TPOT p95 <= 20ms/token, p99 <= 50ms/token; sustained throughput target ~14.4k tokens/sec with error rate < 1% under steady-state, graceful degradation under 2x/5x spikes. any additions?
[06:18] Raj: add that we want per-route dashboards and alerts tied to those SLOs, and CSV export of raw measurements.
[06:26] Maya: noted. we'll deliver dashboards in the console and share raw csvs.
[06:31] Leah: last thing — cost estimates per 1000 tokens for each config.
[06:35] Maya: will include cost estimates across hosted, quantized, and dedicated pool configs.
[06:40] Maya: okay we'll close there, action items assigned. thanks everyone.
[06:45] Raj: thanks all.

End of call.
